correctness.rationale: For an extraspecial group, \(\Phi(G)=Z(G)\) and the Frattini quotient has dimension \(2n\), so Burnside's basis theorem gives \(d(G)=2n\). At \(n=1\), noncommuting images are a basis and therefore generate, making \(\Xi(G)\) edgeless. For \(n\ge2\), no pair generates, so adjacency is exactly nonorthogonality under the nondegenerate commutator form. Projectivizing produces fibers of size \(p(p-1)\); direct hyperplane counting gives the strongly regular parameters, and the tensor-product adjacency matrix gives the stated spectrum. The packaged checker verifies the boundary and representative higher-rank cases from explicit group and symplectic computations.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete exact model for a canonical infinite family in the graph introduced by the primary source, including the sharp rank-one boundary. It replaces a generic diameter-two conclusion by a projective symplectic structure and a closed spectrum, and it shows precisely what the graph remembers and forgets: it recovers the prime and rank but not extraspecial type.
